articles.title: SpaceX Starship test to attempt first-ever spaceship 'catch'
articles.description: Elon Musk's SpaceX was poised Friday to carry out its latest test of the world's biggest and most powerful rocket, the Starship, with plans for a groundbreaking "catch" of the spaceship following a day in orbit.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: SpaceX's Starship undertakes a groundbreaking test attempting the first-ever spaceship 'catch' with the world's biggest and most powerful rocket.

articles.title: A massive new simulation reveals how the universe emerged from darkness
articles.description: A groundbreaking new supercomputer simulation is revealing how the universe escaped its cosmic dark age and transformed into a cosmos filled with stars and galaxies. Called Lumina, it recreates 2 billion years of early cosmic history across a region 1.6 billion light-years wide, capturing extraordinary details that previous simulations could not.
articles.summary: A breakthrough supercomputer simulation reveals how the universe emerged from its cosmic dark age and underwent dramatic transformation.

articles.title: SpaceX launches Starship on ambitious 22-hour Flight 15 test, but aborts booster 'chopsticks' catch (video)
articles.description: SpaceX's Starship megarocket reached orbit today (Nov. 13) during its 15th test flight, but the company scrapped a plan to catch the vehicle's massive booster back at the launch site.
articles.summary: SpaceX's Starship achieves orbit on its 15th test flight, marking continued progress toward full reusability of the megarocket system.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 13, 1971: NASA's Mariner 9 becomes 1st spacecraft to orbit Mars, revealing close looks at the Martian surface
articles.description: On Nov. 13, 1971, Mariner 9 became the first spacecraft to orbit Mars.  Here's why it mattered.
articles.summary: Mariner 9 became the first spacecraft to orbit Mars on November 13, 1971, providing unprecedented close-up views of the Martian surface.

articles.description: Après plus d'un an à scruter les profondeurs du cosmos, le télescope spatial Euclid vient de franchir une étape décisive. Les astrophysiciens du monde entier vont pouvoir explorer une quantité vertigineuse de nouvelles données en plus d'une mosaïque d'images …
articles.summary: The Euclid space telescope discovers 900 million galaxies, opening a cosmic treasure trove that could fundamentally transform our understanding of the universe.

articles.title: Outbursts from a Massive Star
articles.description: Using NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory, astronomers have discovered what is triggering repeated outbursts from a giant, unstable star located in the galaxy shown in this image released on Nov. 9, 2026. The volatile star, known as AT 2016blu, is in the spiral galaxy NGC 4559, located about 30 million light-years from Earth. Astronomers estimate the […]
articles.summary: NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory has revealed the mechanism triggering repeated outbursts from a massive star, advancing our understanding of stellar behavior.

articles.title: Gemini Astronaut Photos Inspired Early Earth Observation Program
articles.description: Astronauts James A. Lovell Jr. and Edwin E. “Buzz” Aldrin Jr. orbited Earth from November 11 to 15, 1966, on Gemini XII, the final mission of NASA’s Gemini program. In addition to successfully completing rendezvous maneuvers and spacewalks, procedures vital to sending American astronauts to the Moon, the crew was also spurring the development of […]
articles.summary: Historic Gemini XII mission photographs by astronauts Lovell and Aldrin inspired the development of early Earth observation programs from space.

articles.title: NASA’s Hubble Offers Cosmic Sampler of Targets for Roman
articles.description: A gallery of gravitational lenses captured by NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope showcases the diversity of this cosmic phenomenon and lays the groundwork for follow-up observations by the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope.
articles.summary: NASA's Hubble Space Telescope has captured a diverse gallery of gravitational lenses that serve as ideal targets for the upcoming Roman Space Telescope.

articles.title: Astrophysicists Cross Another Dark Matter Candidate Off Their List: Stupendously Large Black Holes
articles.description: Astrophysicists are leaving no stone unturned in their search for what dark matter is. Different particles have been proposed, like WIMPs and axions. Hypothetical rimordial black holes have also been proposed. But there's another less well-known candidate, SLABs or Stupendously Large Black holes, a sub-type of primordial black holes. Alas, SLABs can't account for dark matter either, according to new research.
articles.summary: Astrophysicists have ruled out stupendously large black holes as dark matter candidates, narrowing the search for this cosmic mystery.

articles.title: LOFAR Takes the Deepest Image of the Low-Frequency Radio Sky to Date
articles.description: Using the Low Frequency Array (LOFAR), an international team led by Leiden University has produced the sharpest and most sensitive radio image of the sky ever made at low radio frequencies.
articles.summary: The Low Frequency Array (LOFAR) has produced the deepest and sharpest image of the low-frequency radio sky to date, revealing new cosmic insights.

articles.title: Dense Galaxy Clusters Foster Mechanisms That Throttle Star Formation
articles.description: The Cosmic Noon was when the Universe's Stelliferous Era Began, and star formation was prodigious during that epoch. But since then, star formation has slowed to a relative crawl, despite the fact that we can watch them forming in regions throughout the Milky Way. What happened to the hydrogen gas that forms stars? New research found clues in a particulary dense galaxy cluster.
articles.summary: New research explains how dense galaxy clusters regulate star formation mechanisms during the Universe's Cosmic Noon era.

articles.title: Euclid's First Data Release: A Stepping Stone to its 3D Map of the Sky
articles.description: The ESA's Euclid Space Telescope has released its first huge batch of data. It's all part of the telescope's mission to study dark energy and dark matter. The telescope is busy creating the largest ever 3D map of the Universe with its huge 600 megapixel camera, and new images give us some highlights.
articles.summary: The ESA's Euclid Space Telescope releases its first major data batch, advancing its mission to create a comprehensive 3D map of the sky and unlock secrets of dark matter and dark energy.

articles.title: SpaceX's Starship soars into orbit after booster explosion prevents an unprecedented double catch
articles.description: SpaceX's attempt to recover its entire Starship back at the launch pad was thwarted when the booster fell into the Gulf of Mexico and exploded Friday, but the spacecraft still soared into orbit in its boldest test yet.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: SpaceX's Starship achieves orbital flight during an ambitious test that attempted an unprecedented booster catch, marking a major milestone in reusable rocket technology.

articles.title: NASA’s Perseverance confirms a key ingredient for life hidden in ancient Mars rocks
articles.description: NASA's Perseverance rover has confirmed complex organic carbon just beneath the surface of ancient Martian rocks, raising intriguing questions about the Red Planet's potential to have supported life. The remarkable preservation of these compounds, along with similar discoveries thousands of miles away, suggests the building blocks of life may once have been widespread across Mars.
articles.summary: NASA's Perseverance rover confirms complex organic carbon in ancient Martian rocks, strengthening evidence for conditions that could support life.

articles.title: Dark energy may have flipped from negative to positive 9.5 billion years ago
articles.description: A mysterious force driving the expansion of the Universe may have undergone a dramatic reversal billions of years ago. Scientists exploring an overlooked branch of an alternative gravity theory discovered that dark energy could have switched from negative to positive roughly 9.5 billion years ago, potentially changing how we understand cosmic history.
articles.summary: Groundbreaking research suggests dark energy may have reversed from negative to positive expansion approximately 9.5 billion years ago.

articles.title: Earth's fiery birth may have created hundreds of oceans' worth of water
articles.description: Earth's water may have been born in the planet's fiery atmosphere rather than delivered by icy comets or asteroids. Scientists discovered that rocky pebbles reacting with hydrogen under extreme heat can produce water in minutes, potentially generating hundreds of oceans' worth during Earth's formation. The findings suggest that water may be a natural part of how rocky planets form, rather than something that must arrive from space.
articles.summary: Scientists discover that Earth's water may have originated in the planet's early atmosphere rather than arriving via comets or asteroids.

articles.title: NASA offers $500,000 to develop next-generation electric rocket engines
articles.description: NASA is putting $500,000 on the line in a new competition to accelerate the development of advanced electric rocket engines for satellites and future space exploration. The AMPERE Challenge will reward up to two U.S. companies with cash prizes and access to NASA testing facilities to help bring promising propulsion technology closer to real-world missions.
articles.summary: NASA awards $500,000 in funding to accelerate development of next-generation electric propulsion systems for advanced spacecraft.

articles.title: 100 launches! Rocket Lab sends Earth-observing satellite to orbit on milestone mission (photos)
articles.description: Rocket Lab launched its 100th space mission shortly after midnight on Saturday (Nov. 14), sending a private Japanese Earth-observing satellite to orbit.
articles.summary: Rocket Lab celebrates its 100th space launch with a successful Earth-observation satellite mission for a private Japanese operator.

articles.title: California's brand-new Air & Space Center, home of the space shuttle Endeavour, opens today
articles.description: The California Science Center's brand-new Samuel Oschin Air & Space Center —the home of NASA's space shuttle Endeavour —officially opened to the public today (Nov. 13).
articles.summary: California's new Samuel Oschin Air & Space Center opens to the public as the permanent home of the space shuttle Endeavour.

articles.title: Scientists discover mysterious radio signals coming every eight minutes from deep space
articles.description: Astronomers in have linked the regular radio pulses to an unusual pairing of celestial bodies 5,000 light-years from Earth.
articles.summary: Astronomers identify the source of mysterious regular radio pulses occurring every eight minutes from an unusual celestial object 5,000 light-years away.

articles.summary: Astronomers solve the mystery of exoplanet TOI-2535 b, which vanished from observations after seven years of monitoring.

articles.summary: SpaceX approaches a crucial test flight that could bring the company closer to achieving the 'holy grail' of rocketry through revolutionary spaceflight capabilities.

articles.title: Asteroid Bennu's Sample Delivers Another Surprise
articles.description: Researchers compared the samples from asteroid Bennu with the Murchison meteorite and measured the amino acid β-alanine in both. Using new techniques, they were able to measure not only their isotopic compositions, but isotopic differences between individual …
articles.summary: Analysis of samples from asteroid Bennu reveals the presence of amino acid β-alanine, providing insights into the chemical composition and origins of solar system materials.

articles.description: Quatre ans après que la NASA a volontairement écrasé un engin sur un astéroïde, nous avons enfin une vue en gros plan des dégâts !
